description: Labelled ground truth for the 13-repo wild corpus (Express + NestJS boilerplates, 1,900 files). Same contract as edge-ground-truth.json: every class carries an adjudicated verdict, FP classes must reach zero, and an UNLABELLED class fails --strict so untriaged findings can never silently become the published FP number.
method: A finding's class is its rule plus the shape of the offending expression with identifiers erased — the unit at which one rule change resolves every member. FP = the rule should not fire on this shape; the class is a bug and must reach zero. TP = the rule is right and the finding belongs upstream. Every verdict must cite a measurement or a named file:line, never an impression.
corpus: 13 repositories, all 1K+ stars, recommended presets only

classes.reason: Deprecated rule (meta.deprecated=true, replacedBy require-csrf-protection) that was still in `recommended` at 'warn' alongside its replacement at 'error'. 21 of these locations were reported by both rules at once. Removed from the preset; the rule stays exported.

Detection is correct — every one of these files creates an Express app and genuinely mounts no rate limiter. But 27 of 30 are express/examples/*, 20-line demos of a single feature, where the advice is true and not actionable. Already 'warn' in recommended, which is the right severity for a class that fires once per app-creating file with identical advice. Not an FP; do not silence.

Same shape as require-rate-limiting: correct detection, 27 of 29 on express/examples/*. Sits at 'error' while its sibling sits at 'warn' — that inconsistency is the actionable part, not the detection.

Measured on the 13-repo corpus: 27 of 33 findings compare something secret-shaped, including three confirmed upstream bugs — express-mongoose-es6-rest-api auth.controller.js:22 (`req.body.password === user.password`, plaintext and timing-unsafe), express/examples/auth/index.js:70 (`hash === user.hash`), bulletproof-nodejs config/index.ts:51 (hardcoded `password: '123456'`). The 6 misses are enum/env comparisons where the rule keys off an identifier containing "auth" rather than the compared value being a secret; that is a precision bug inside a TP class, not an FP class.

express/lib/view.js:201 `fs.statSync(path)`, lib/boot.js:14 `fs.readdirSync(dir)` — library internals with no request-derived input. The rule has no notion of a trust boundary, which its own recommended-preset comment already documents, and it ships at 'warn' for exactly this reason. Correct by its own definition; low yield.

Not because CSRF does not matter, but because every one of these 19 locations is also reported by express-security/no-missing-csrf-protection — 19/19 overlap, two rules in one plugin firing on one condition, two errors on one line, and silencing either leaves the other. One of the pair must defer.

1 confirmed upstream true positive: bulletproof-nodejs/src/config/index.ts:51 `password: '123456'` in a 5.8K-star boilerplate. The other 17 are all in express-rest-boilerplate/integration/auth.test.js — real fixture credentials in a file matching *.test.js, which `allowInTests` should already skip. Needs investigation: either the option is not applied on this path or its pattern misses `integration/*.test.js`.

What remains after PR #457 is genuine unescaped interpolation into HTML — `'
  • ' + user.name + '
    • '` in express/examples/content-negotiation, `req.session.views` in examples/session. Express itself fixes this exact class with escapeHtml elsewhere in the same tree (examples/route-map/index.js:47), so the finding is actionable and correct. The 28 authored-text and already-escaped findings that used to sit in this class are gone.

12 -> 1. Two root causes, both name-as-evidence. (a) Any recovery-named variable whose initializer did not textually contain one of four hardcoded generator names was 'predictable', so `const forgotPassword = catchAsync(...)` (a route handler) and `generateToken(...)` (an opaque project helper) both reported; predictability must now be shown — Math.random, Date.now, new Date().getTime, time-based uuid v1. (b) Function-level checks matched the function NAME alone, so ack-nestjs-boilerplate's Swagger decorators UserPublicForgotPasswordDoc/UserPublicResetPasswordDoc drew four findings telling a doc generator to add token expiry and rate limiting; a function whose whole body is one `return` performs no recovery flow. One finding remains: weakRecoveryVerification on `if (!resetPasswordEmail)` in a seed template, a null guard.

`app.use(express.urlencoded())` and `app.use(express.json())` with no `limit` option — the default is 100kb for json but urlencoded without extended/limit is a genuine unbounded-payload risk. Real finding, actionable in one line, and it lands on node-express-boilerplate/src/app.js:28 as well as the demos.

CLOSED. The rule reported any string containing the WORD password/token/secret, so prose was a finding: `throw new Error('Token not found')`, `throw new Error('Invalid token type')`, and a message quoting a password policy back to the user. A standalone literal must now carry a value (`<word><separator><value>`), while the identifier path keeps the plain word match because a variable named `password` is sensitive for what it holds. 10 -> 0, no TP lost. The fix also closed a pre-existing false negative: the logging path handled Literal and Identifier arguments but not a concatenation of the two, so `console.log('password: ' + password)` — the case this rule most exists for — was silent.

All 10 are express/examples/* demo routes (`app.get('/users', user.list)`). An unauthenticated GET in a feature demo is intended. Same class as require-helmet: correct detection, wrong context, and not distinguishable statically.

CLOSED. The ZIP-bomb branch matched the callee's printed text for the bare substring 'Extract' and reported unconditionally, so passport-jwt's `ExtractJwt.fromAuthHeaderAsBearerToken()` was flagged as an unbounded decompression in four repos. Decompression is now matched structurally, with the receiver resolved through its import/require binding rather than by name — `const unzip = require('unzipper')` still reports. 9 -> 0 on the wild corpus, no TP lost.

Zero XPath exists anywhere in the corpus. The rule now gates on XPATH_SYNTAX over literalTextOf, but that pattern matches `://` and `::`, so every URL template and namespaced key qualifies: `${env.app.schema}://${host}:${port}`, `nats://${host}:${port}`, `${domain}::${req.userId}`. `://` is close to the most common substring in any codebase. Needs a real XPath sink (evaluate/selectNodes/XPathEvaluator), not a syntax guess.

note: Verdicts: FP = the rule should not fire on this shape, the class is a bug and must reach zero. TP = the rule is right and the finding belongs upstream. TP-ADVISORY = detection is correct but the finding is advice rather than a vulnerability in context; these are not silenced and not counted as FPs. MIXED = the class contains both and must be split before it can be closed. The target is zero FALSE positives, not zero findings — a corpus with no findings would mean we stopped looking.
